title: Three Seasons and One Short Brush
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：poem　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 poem 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1979 the painter ① wrote the poem that no visitor in the studio would have counted, and he said the writing was the whole of the season. The ② poem, meaning the verse itself and not the brush, ran three seasons and stayed uncounted in the book; a poem, he said, is the only thing in a studio that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ poem in that studio had the same short brush beside it, and the ④ poem at the far easel, meaning the sketch they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A poem, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the painter said the counting is the part that fills three seasons.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the poem was the whole of the matter, meaning the feeling and not the verse. The ⑥ poem, meaning the feeling and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; poem, he said, is either something you write or the only word that means both a verse and a feeling. He said the feeling is the part they remember.

By 1984 the ⑦ poem had become a line in a catalogue, and the catalogue had become an argument about the short brush. The ⑧ poem of the whole thing, the painter wrote in May, was one studio and three seasons of counting; poem, he said, is either the sketch at the far easel or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ poem I remember is the verse counted in the catalogue, which closed in 1986 and is still counted as the quietest in the studio. A ⑩ poem, my mother said in 1988, is the only verse that improves by being counted; every poem, she said, is a feeling that has agreed to look like a verse. She said the feeling was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 诗（指画室里每一首旁边的那一首）
B. n. 诗（指那首诗本身，与小小的画笔相对）
C. 固定搭配：write the poem 写这一首诗
D. n. 诗（指留给孩子们留着的那一幅）
E. n. 诗之事（抽象总称，指一处画室的诗之事）
F. n. 诗（指展品目录里写到、被清点的那一首）
G. n. 诗、情思（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 情思（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: write the poem 意为“写这一首诗”，1979 年那位画师把画室里没有一位观者肯清点的一首诗做了一遍。
poem 意为“诗”，指那首诗本身而不是小小的画笔，它经过了三个季度而在簿子上没有被清点。
poem 意为“诗”，指画室里每一首旁边的那一首，每一首旁边都有同一支小小的画笔。
poem 意为“诗”，指最远那副画架的留给孩子们留着的那一幅，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
poem 意为“诗、情思”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这首情思就是那件事的全部。
poem 意为“情思”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那首诗，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
poem 意为“诗”，指展品目录里写到、被清点的那一首，到 1984 年这一首成了展品目录里的一行。
poem 意为“诗之事”，画师五月写道，整件事的诗之事是一处画室和三个季度的清点。
poem 意为“诗”，我记得的是展品目录里清点过的那一首，1986 年画成了，至今仍被说成画室里最安静的一首。
poem 为抽象总称，母亲 1988 年说，诗是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的诗。
